walkthroughs.body_html:
The UK government spends roughly:

  • ~25% on health (NHS).
  • ~20% on pensions and welfare.
  • ~10% on education.
  • ~5% on defence.
  • Plus transport, housing, debt interest.

The Chancellor of the Exchequer writes the budget once a year.

They decide whether to raise or cut taxes, and where the money goes. The Budget speech is famous — held up in a red box. 📦

Spending is full of choices:

  • More schools or more hospitals?
  • Lower tax or higher benefits?
  • Save the planet now or grow the economy?

Every choice has winners and losers. ⚖️

mcqs.q: What does the assumption 'ceteris paribus' mean in economic models?
options: 'All other things equal' — when analysing the effect of one variable, all other variables are held constant. It is an analytical simplification, not a claim about reality.
Ceteris paribus means everything happens at the same time in real markets.
Ceteris paribus is a Latin name for the equilibrium price.
